title: Three windows of saying nothing
spec: M13 · corroboration, sustain, and the alert that does not fire
intro: A drift signal crosses its threshold in window 41 and the detector stays silent. A second signal joins it and it stays silent again. The alert only fires in window 44 — and the three silences are the part of this detector that is hard to build and impossible to draw as a static example.

provenance.source: a narrated four-window drift trace over prior-auth traffic, run against M13's check_drift(); PSI, embedding-shift, override and judge readings are plausible inventions, not measurements

foot: This walks M13's A Label-Free Drift Detector — four signals, the len(firing) >= 2 corroboration rule, and sustained(firing, n=3).

steps.title: Window 41 — one signal fires, nothing happens
narrative: The detector runs on six-hour windows of prior-auth traffic, roughly 30,000 determinations each. In window 41, PSI(baseline.features, window.features) comes back at 0.19 against a 0.15 threshold. Input drift, unambiguously: the shape of incoming requests has moved.
firing has one element in it. The rule is len(firing) >= 2 and sustained(firing, n=3), so alert_drift() is not called and nobody is paged.

This is the correct behaviour and it is the hardest behaviour to hold onto, because a single PSI breach looks exactly like the beginning of a real problem. It is also what a Monday volume bump, a holiday mix shift, and one large provider group submitting a batch all look like. Firing here is how drift alerts get muted.
steps.youDo: Pull your last quarter of drift alerts and count how many were single-signal. That share is the fraction of pages your team learned to ignore.
steps.claudeSays: One threshold crossed. The rule requires two, so the function returned the signal dictionary and did nothing else. Silence here is a decision, not an oversight.

terminal.text:
input_psi   0.19   threshold 0.15   FIRING
emb_shift   0.11   threshold 0.25   ok
override    0.064  threshold 0.082  ok
judge_drop  4.29   threshold 4.16   ok
no alert  (rule: len(firing) >= 2 and sustained(firing, n=3))

steps.title: Windows 42 and 43 — two signals, still silent
narrative: In window 42 the PSI climbs to 0.22 and EmbeddingShift joins it at 0.27, over its 0.25 threshold. Two signals now corroborate: the incoming request features moved and the embeddings of the clinical notes moved with them. That is a much stronger claim than either alone.
len(firing) >= 2 is satisfied. sustained(firing, n=3) is not — this is one window, and the rule wants three consecutive. Silence again.

Window 43 makes it two: PSI 0.24, embedding shift 0.30, and the override rate starting to lean at 0.078 without yet crossing 0.082. Still silent, and by now the temptation to lower n is real. Hold it. Two windows is twelve hours, and twelve hours of movement is still inside the range that a single large provider onboarding produces and then stops producing.
steps.claudeSays: Corroboration and sustain are two different guards. The first says several independent measurements agree; the second says the agreement survived time. A detector with only the first pages on every correlated blip.
steps.youDo: Set n from your window length and your tolerable detection lag, not from taste. Six-hour windows with n=3 means you accept an eighteen-hour lag in exchange for silence on anything shorter.

terminal.text:
input_psi   0.22   FIRING
emb_shift   0.27   FIRING
override    0.069  ok
judge_drop  4.27   ok

input_psi   0.24   FIRING
emb_shift   0.30   FIRING
override    0.078  ok  (leaning)
judge_drop  4.22   ok  (leaning)
firing len=2   sustained_run=2   -> still no alert, 2 of 3 windows

after.title: AFTER — window 43, the run is building

steps.title: Window 44 — the run closes and the alert fires
narrative: Third consecutive window. PSI 0.26, embedding shift 0.33 — and now the proxy-quality signals cross too. Reviewer override is at 0.091 against a 0.082 threshold, and the live judge score has fallen to 4.13, under 4.16.
That is four of four firing, on the third consecutive window. len(firing) >= 2 and sustained(firing, n=3) are both true, and alert_drift(firing, signals) runs.

The order the signals arrived in is the diagnosis. Inputs moved first, then the note embeddings, then extraction quality, then the judge — that is input drift propagating into output quality, not a model swap and not a policy change. The alert ships with the story attached: a new provider group onboarded on the 19th, submitting 2,100 notes a day in a template the bundle's few-shot examples have never seen.
steps.claudeSays: Four signals firing, three windows running, one page. The detector waited eighteen hours to say something it can defend.
steps.youDo: Make your alert carry firing and the full signals dict, not just a boolean. Which signals moved and in what order is most of the root cause, and it is free.

emb_shift   0.33   threshold 0.25   FIRING
override    0.091  threshold 0.082  FIRING
judge_drop  4.13   threshold 4.16   FIRING

PSI contribution: 71% from submitter_group=NORTHSHORE_ORTHO (onboarded 08-19)

after.title: AFTER — window 44, the rule is satisfied

steps.title: What the three silences bought
narrative: Eighteen hours from first signal to page. That sounds slow until you price the alternative: the nurse-confirmed labels that would prove this drift arrive nineteen days later, through the appeals pipeline, by which time roughly 2.3 million determinations have gone through the drifted bundle.

Now price the other alternative. Set the rule to fire on any single signal and re-run the quarter: it would have paged 14 times, and 13 of those are Monday volume bumps, a holiday mix shift, and two batch re-deliveries. The fourteenth is this one. A detector with a 7% precision gets muted by the third week, and then it catches nothing at all.

The corroboration-and-sustain rule is not a compromise between sensitivity and noise. It is the thing that keeps the detector installed — and an alert nobody has muted is the only kind that detects anything.
steps.claudeSays: The interesting output of this detector across four windows was three non-alerts. Nothing in a static screenshot of window 44 tells you that the restraint was there.
steps.youDo: Replay your own drift rule against last quarter and count the pages it would have produced. If it is more than about one a month, your team will mute it before it is ever right.

items.note: fires instantly, and 13 of 14 times it is wrong — muted by week 3

view.text: A drift detector is judged on the alerts it declines to send. Require several independent signals to agree, require the agreement to survive N windows, and ship the firing list with the page so the responder gets the drift type for free. Labels are the ground truth and they are also three weeks late — label-free corroboration is what turns that into eighteen hours.
